This Miscellaneous First Appeal coming on for Admission through Physical Hearing/Video Conferencing, this day, the Court delivered the following:
 JUDGMENT

The present appeal is filed by the claimant under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988,
seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the learned II Addl.
Senior

Civil Judge and Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Hassan, (hereinafter for brevity referred to as 'the Tribunal'), in its judgment and award dated 28.01.2020, in M.V.C.No.203/2019.
2.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The summary of the case of the present appellant as claimant before the Tribunal was that, on the date 02.07.2018, in the afternoon at about 2.00 p.m., while the claimant was going on his motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-46-J-7192, from Hassan Town towards Tanniruhalla, near Santhepete Circle, a Tractor with Trailer bearing registration No.KA-17-TA-7289, being driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, came from behind and dashed to the motorcycle of the claimant, due to which road traffic accident, the claimant fell down and sustained multiple grievous injuries to his right shoulder, head and other parts of the body.

The claimant has stated that,
thereafter, he was shifted to Government Hospital, Hassan and from there, he was taken to a private hospital i.e., Janapriaya Hospital, Hassan, wherein he was admitted as an inpatient and underwent surgery.
The claimant has stated that, he has spent a sum of `1 lakh towards medical expenses.

Prior to the accident, he was working in a private school and cloth shop and earning a sum of `25,000/-,
however, because of the injuries suffered by him, he could not able to continue his job as prior to the Gali Pasha @ Galib Pasha vs Syeed Abdul Farid on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6119168/
2 accident.

sentences.text: With this, he claimed compensation of a sum of `10 lakhs, from respondent Nos.1 and 2 before the Tribunal, who are owner and insurer of the offending Tractor respectively.

3. In response to the notice, both the respondents appeared before the Tribunal and filed their statement of objections, wherein, respondent No.1 has stated that, at the time of the accident, the Tractor was covered with insurance with respondent No.2-Insurance Company, as such, respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation, if any.

On the other hand, the respondent No.2-Insurance Company in its statement of objections denied the manner of occurrence of the accident and the alleged medical expenses said to have been incurred by the claimant.
It also denied the alleged disability said to have been suffered by the claimant.
With this, it prayed to dismiss the claim petition.
Before the Tribunal, the claimant got himself examined as PW-1 and also examined one Dr.Abdul Basheer as PW-2 and got marked documents from Exs.P-1 to P-14.

On behalf of the respondents,
neither any witness was examined nor any documents were produced.

4. After analysing the evidence and the materials placed before it, the Tribunal has awarded the compensation under the following heads with the sum shown against them:

5. The Tribunal awarded compensation of a sum of `2,75,300/- with interest at `8%
per annum thereupon from the date of petition till the date of realisation, holding the owner and Insurer jointly and severally liable to pay the said compensation and directed the Insurer to deposit the award amount.
It is against the said judgment and award passed by the Tribunal, the claimant has filed this appeal seeking enhancement of compensation.
6. The respondent No.2 herein (insurer) is represented by its counsel.

Notice to respondent No.1 is dispensed with vide Court order dated 09.03.2023.
7.
Though this appeal is posted for admission, with the consent from both parties, the matter was taken up for arguments on main on merits.

Learned counsel for the appellant further submits that, he has the copies of the pleadings,
depositions and exhibits, as such, summoning of the trial Court records is also not required and that he would place those copies before the Court.

With this, he places the copies of the pleadings,
depositions and exhibits for a perusal and their return to him.
8. In the light of the above, heard the arguments of learned counsel for the appellant and learned counsel for respondent No.2-Insurance Company.

Perused the materials placed before this Court,
including memorandum of appeal, impugned judgment and also the copies of the pleadings,
depositions and exhibits placed before the Court by the learned counsel for the appellant.

9. The present appeal being the claimant's appeal and respondent No.2 (insurer) having not preferred either cross-objection or a counter appeal, the question of occurrence of accident on the date, time and place as alleged by the claimant and also the alleged rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle is not in dispute.
Further, the claimant got himself examined as PW-1, in his examination-in-chief filed in the form of affidavit evidence has reiterated the contentions taken up by him in his claim petition.

In his support, he got produced and marked the documents from Exs.P-1 to P-14, which inter alia includes copies of FIR, complaint, scene of offence panchanama, Motor Vehicle Inspector's report, wound certificate, charge sheet and discharge summary.

The evidence of PW-1 that the road traffic accident as alleged by him has occurred in the manner as contended in the claim petition due to the sole rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Tractor with Trailer is further corroborated with the FIR, Motor Vehicle Inspector's report and the charge sheet.
The charge sheet at Ex.P-7 accuses the driver of the Tractor for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 337 and 338 of Indian Penal Code, 1860.
The wound certificate shows that the claimant had sustained three simple injuries and one grievous injury in the road traffic accident.

As such, the occurrence of the road traffic accident and the present appellant sustaining injuries in the said road traffic accident and also of the fact that the said road traffic accident occurred at the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Tractor with Trailer bearing registration No.KA-17-TA-7289, stands established.

Therefore, the question of occurrence of accident and the Gali Pasha @ Galib Pasha vs Syeed Abdul Farid on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6119168/

sentences.text: alleged liability of the respondent-Insurance Company to pay compensation to the injured claimant for the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident need not be re-analysed again.

As such,
the only question that remains to be considered is about the quantification of the compensation,
which according to the claimant/appellant is inadequate.

10. The learned counsel for the appellant (claimant) in his argument submitted that though in the memorandum of appeal, he has taken a contention that the compensation under all heads are meagre, however, he confines only with respect to quantification of compensation with respect to loss of income during laid up period and the future loss of income.
He submitted that since the claimant has produced the Salary Certificate, the Tribunal ought to have considered the same.
Even otherwise, the Tribunal has to consider the notional - 10 - income of the claimant at `12,500/- per month since the accident has occurred in the year 2018.

11. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.2- Insurance Company in his argument submitted that the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal being reasonable and just compensation, the same does not warrant interference at the hands of this Court.
He also contends that the rate of interest ordered is also on the higher side.

12. The evidence of the claimant as PW-1, which is further corroborated by the evidence of Dr.Abdul Basheer, who claims to be an Orthopaedic Surgeon working in Janapriya Hospital, Hassan, coupled with the wound certificate at Ex.P-6, the discharge summary at Ex.P-8, would go to show that in the road traffic accident, the claimant sustained fracture of right scapula, injury over right elbow, chest injury and laceration on the right shoulder.
The doctor has opined that the fracture of right scapula was grievous in nature and remaining injuries were simple in nature.
The discharge summary also go to - 11 - show that he was treated as inpatient in Janapriya Hospital, Hassan for a period of six days from 02.07.2018 to 08.07.2018.
It is considering these aspects, since the Tribunal has awarded compensation of a sum of `40,000/- towards pain and suffering, the same being reasonable, I do not find any reason to modify the same.

13. Though the claimant has stated that he has incurred medical expenses of a sum of `1 lakhs,
however, he could able to produce the medical bills and receipts and marked them at Ex.P-9, the total amount of which comes to `67,140/-, as such, the Tribunal has rightly awarded a sum of `67,140/- towards medical expenses.

14. Considering the length of the claimant being inpatient in the hospital and the nature of the injuries suffered by him, the Tribunal after noticing that he must have been attended with an assistance of an attendant and had incurred expenses towards diet and conveyance, since has Gali Pasha @ Galib Pasha vs Syeed Abdul Farid on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6119168/
5 awarded a reasonable compensation of a sum of `20,000/- under the said head, the same does not warrant any interference at the hands of this Court.

sentences.text: - 12 - 15. Towards loss of amenities, after noticing the nature of the injuries suffered by the claimant, the Tribunal has awarded compensation of a sum of `20,000/- which is reasonable, the same does not warrant any revisit by this Court.
16. The claimant has stated that at the time of the road traffic accident, he was working in a cloth shop in Hassan and was earning a sum of `25,000/- per month as salary.
The claimant in his evidence as PW-1 has stated that he was working as Manager in Gouse Mohinuddin Memorial School and was also working in a cloth shop and thus earning a sum of `25,000/- per month.
In support of his contention, he has got produced a letter in a letterhead at EXP.11 alleged to be of Gouse Mohinuddin Memorial School showing that his salary was `15,000/- per month.

However,
the respondents have seriously disputed the alleged income of the claimant.
Admittedly, the author of Ex.P-11 was not examined by the claimant nor he has produced any document to establish his alleged income from working in - 13 - a cloth shop.

Hence, noticing the absence of the same, the Tribunal though has decided to take notional income of the claimant, however, in the said process, it has taken `9,000/- per month as notional income of the claimant at the time of the accident.

Since the accident has occurred in the year 2018 and large number of Motor Accident Claims Tribunals in the State have been taking the notional income at `12,500/- per month for the relevant year, the Tribunal ought to have considered the income of the claimant also at `12,500/- per month.

As such, for the loss of income for a period of two months laid up period, the claimant though was entitled for compensation of a sum of `25,000/-, since the Tribunal has awarded only a sum of `18,000/- in that regard, the claimant is entitled for differential amount of `7,000/- as enhancement under the said head.
17. The claimant has stated that because of the injuries sustained by him in the accident, he is unable to continue his avocation as prior to the accident.

In order to - 14 - support his contention, he got examined the doctor as PW-2, who in his evidence has stated about he assessing the disability of the claimant at 18% to the right upper limb and 6% to the whole body.
It is accepting the said evidence of the witness, the Tribunal has taken the disability at 6% to the wholebody and computed the loss of future income of the claimant.
However, in the said process, it has taken the income of the claimant at `9,000/- per month, when in fact, it was required to take the same at `12,500/- per month.

sentences.text: As stated by the claimant and further as could be seen from the wound certificate at Ex.P-6 and discharge summary at Ex.P-8, the age of the claimant at the time of the accident was rightly taken by the Tribunal as 27 years, as such, the proper multiplier applicable is `17' in the matter.
Thus, the recalculation of the compensation towards `loss of future income' would come to `12,500/- x 12 x 17 x 6/100 = `1,53,000/-.
Since the Tribunal has awarded compensation of a sum of `1,10,160/-, the - 15 - claimant is entitled for a differential amount of `42,840/- under the head of `loss of future income'.
18. Barring the above, the claimant/appellant is not entitled for compensation under any other heads or for enhancement of compensation under any other heads.

Thus, in total the appellant is entitled for the modified compensation as below :
